steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Genre hybridity is the combination of conventions from two or more distinct genres within a single film, creating a new blended category.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Sub-genres are more specific categories within a broader genre, such as slasher horror within horror or space opera within science fiction.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Genre mixing has become increasingly common in contemporary cinema as studios seek to attract wider and more diverse audiences.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Postmodern genre theory argues that in a media-saturated culture, pure genres no longer exist — all contemporary films are to some extent hybrid.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: When analysing a hybrid film, identify the parent genres and which conventions come from each — then explain what the combination achieves. Distinguish between parody, pastiche and genuine hybridity: each has a different relationship with genre convention. Use theoretical frameworks — Jameson, Neale — to give your analysis depth and show understanding beyond simple identification. Consider why the filmmaker chose hybridity: what does the combination allow that a single genre would not? Discuss audience response to hybridity: does the blend satisfy or frustrate genre expectations, and what meaning does that create?
